# Foreword and introduction {.unnumbered}

**Eimear:**

Conducting a research study is not easy. By definition, we are attempting to generate knowledge that was previously unknown. This means that there are no easy answers and the path from idea to completion is often forked or obscured. There is a lot to think about, a lot of moving parts and a lot of conflicting advice. Our idea with this book was to attempt to bring some clarity and direction to the process. To provide an accessible resource to allow new researchers to form a plan, to clarify their position on key concepts and to recognize the complexity and nuance that is inherent to the research process.

The book contains 9 chapters, each one focusing on a distinct aspect of the research process, from broader philosophy, to designing your research question, to selecting participants and defining your collection and analysis plan. They are arranged sequentially and we encourage you to read it from start to finish, however each chapter can also work as a stand-alone, so feel free to dip in and out if that is what you prefer. As you read the book, you will notice that the chapters follow very different styles. When inviting experts, we did not dictate a style or content, but left it to each author team to determine what was most appropriate for their own chapter, topic and style. I believe there is a valuable lesson to be learned from this variation. There are multiple ways to approach the research process and complex problems should be tackled from many angles. Our goal is not to provide a definitive to-do list, but instead to provide a guide that can empower you to approach the process in a logical way and to help you to develop your ability to make informed and justified decisions.

Thank you for choosing to read our book -- we really hope you find it useful.

I wish you all the best in your research journey,

Eimear
